title: Schmigadoon! is finally on Broadway and it’s glorious #Schmigadoon #B...
transcript: Schmigadoon is now on Broadway, which in many ways feels like where it was always meant to be. I obviously love the Apple TV Show that it is based on. I was also lucky enough to see it at the Kennedy Center, which I also loved, but was very much a concert production. And honestly, one of my biggest concerns with this transfer was that they would just take the Kennedy Center concert production and plop it on a Broadway stage. After all, the last show to transfer from the Kennedy Center was spamalot, and that was very much my issue with that production. The cast was fantastic, but the production itself just did not feel Broadway caliber, which is why I am so excited to say that they gave schmigadoon the proper Broadway glow up that it deserves. The set features these gorgeous hand painted drops that you really don't see anymore, and it feels like a throwback to classic Broadway, which is exactly what it should feel like. Schmigadoon is a love letter to the classic Golden Age musicals, and the production reflects that. As for the script itself, it is very much the TV Show on stage. Pretty much all of the songs from the TV Show are in here and are gorgeously recreated by Chris Gattelli, who actually did the choreography on the TV Show and is directing and choreographing schmigadoon on Broadway. There are a handful of new songs As well, most notably a marry the man today-esque duet between Florence and Melissa, which sadly replaces he's a queer one, that man o mine from the TV Show, which is a song that I love, but this new song is very good and very fun. There is also a new song for Betsy, Mckenzie Kurtz's character, and a duet between mayor Menlove, and the pastor. But besides these handful of moments, it is very much just the TV Show on stage, for better or worse. So if you didn't like the TV Show, I don't think you're gonna like it on Broadway. But if you liked the TV Show, I do think you're gonna like it on Broadway. There are certainly some pacing issues that arise from taking a six episode TV Series and crunching it down into a two and a half hour musical. But season one of Schmigadoon is pretty short. It only runs about three hours if you binge the whole thing, so there isn't really much that they needed to cut in order to make it a musical. I also wanna shout out the cast, who I think is universally excellent. Stand out in my opinion being Sara Chase as Melissa, who legitimately should be in the conversation for Best Lead Actress at the Tonys. She's that good. But it is an ensemble of Broadway vets and they are all bringing It from Brad Oscar, Anna Gasteyer, Alex Brightman, Mckenzie Kurtz, Izzy McCalla, Max Clayton. You also have Anne Herrada recreating the role that she played on the TV Show, which is so, so fun. The entire cast is absolutely bringing it. And if you are a fan of musicals, I'm going to say that Schmigadoon is a Broadway Ben must see.
classificationReason: Creator shares first-hand opinions on the Broadway transfer, praising hand-painted sets, script fidelity to the TV show, and the 'glow up' from the Kennedy Center concert production.
